Situation1: Your friend has misunderstood the tone of your text message and replied sounding hurt. You need to call them right now to explain.
Situation2: They skim a recent pharmacy newsletter while on break to see what new drugs have been released.
Story:
I glanced at my phone during my lunch break, just as I was about to open the latest pharmacy newsletter. My friend’s name flashed on the screen, their message sharp and short: “Didn’t expect that from you.” My heart dropped. I reread my earlier text, realizing how my rushed words could have sounded cold. I knew I should call them right away, clear things up before the misunderstanding grew. That’s what a good friend would do—communicate, not let hurt fester.

But the newsletter sat open on my computer, full of updates on new medications and safety alerts. I’d promised myself I’d stay current, especially after missing last month’s issue. My manager always emphasized how important it was to keep up, and I didn’t want to fall behind. I felt the pressure of both roles—my friend needed me now, but so did my profession. My thumb hovered over the call button, my eyes flicking between the phone and the glowing screen, torn between the expectations of being a good friend and a responsible pharmacist.
